clue.text: Where one may see wild birds, not big game

definitions.text: Where one may see wild birds

parts.note: something not big is slim, thin
bridge is the card game

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher's tip: go for the wildfowl rather than hunting large animals.
explanation.walkthrough: SLIMBRIDGE, in Gloucestershire, England, is the Wildfowl and Wetlands Trust's best-known reserve. 'big game' reads as hunting, but 'game' is the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gloucestershire reserve founded by Peter Scott is famous for its flocks of swans, geese and ducks.

clue.text: Well wrapped up, so was in no hurry

definitions.meaning: pipes or a boiler insulated with lagging are thoroughly wrapped
to lag is to fall behind or dawdle

explanation.surface: Someone dressed warmly and so taking their time.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is insulated with lagging material; the other is dawdled or fell behind.

clue.text: On the verge of alarming changes

indicators.note: changes signals that the letters of the word before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A situation close to dramatic, alarming developments.
explanation.definitionFit: Marginal means at the margin or edge, so only just in or out.

clue.text: Dealing with purchase's withdrawal

parts.note: re means concerning or dealing with
purchase means grip, which is traction

explanation.surface: A buyer handles the cancellation of a purchase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purchase' means grip or leverage here, not buying.
explanation.definitionFit: A retraction is a taking back of a statement, a withdrawal of it.

clue.text: A politician retreats outside and gets wet

indicators.note: outside means the word for retreats goes around the a and politician

parts.note: dens are private retreats
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician escapes the rain by retreating indoors but is soaked anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: Here it means makes wet, moistens, as rain does to clothes.

clue.text: Drink up before noon and dash

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for drink is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ale is a drink

explanation.surface: Down a drink before midday and rush off.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash means flair or panache, a lively style.

clue.text: Left one cat a vital form of access

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a feline is a cat

explanation.surface: A will leaving a cat a crucial means of support.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope or connection that keeps someone in reach of help is their vital link.

clue.text: Put back in office, as the controller said

parts.note: a rein is used to control a horse
stated means said

explanation.surface: A minister restored to their post, according to the controller's announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as the' is only a link here, joining the definition to the two side-by-side pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate someone is to restore them to a former position.

clue.text: Raised in family of wolves

indicators.note: in tells us the word for raised sits inside the word for family

parts.note: a line is a family lineage
raised means up

explanation.surface: A child brought up among a pack of wolves, like Mowgli.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective comes from Latin lupus, wolf, so it means wolflike or relating to wolves.

clue.text: Plant amateur gardener's first to change

indicators.note: the letters are made to change their order, signalling a rearrangement
first asks for only the opening letter of gardener's

explanation.surface: A novice gardener's first plant is about to be altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges AMATEUR plus G, the first letter of 'gardener's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageratum is a garden annual with fluffy blue flowers, also called floss flower.

clue.text: Criticise article about ancient Roman building

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
the is the definite article
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A critic writes a hostile piece about a classical Roman monument.
explanation.definitionFit: The domed temple to all the gods in Rome, rebuilt under Hadrian, still stands.

clue.text: Port is a place of safety

parts.note: a den is a lair or retreat where one is safe

explanation.surface: A harbour described as a safe haven.
explanation.definitionFit: Aden is the seaport city of Yemen at the mouth of the Red Sea.

clue.text: A lofty paper provided on every occasion

parts.note: lofty means tall
The Times is a newspaper

explanation.surface: A highbrow newspaper is always on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means always, without exception.

clue.text: Check on tax in court

indicators.note: in places the words for on and tax within the abbreviation for court

parts.note: taken as written
to tax something is to put strain on it

explanation.surface: A tax inspection held in a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: A check, as on spending, is a restriction or limit placed on it.

clue.text: To the Continental an allowance shows indulgence

parts.note: le is the French for the
a ration is a fixed allowance

explanation.surface: A Continental allowance displays lenience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Continental' means 'the' in a European language: LE in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Toleration is a patient permissiveness, putting up with things.

clue.text: About to enter a plea for approval

indicators.note: to enter means the abbreviation for about goes inside the phrase a plea

parts.note: a claim is a plea or demand
C, from Latin circa, is the abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: A petitioner is about to submit an application for approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enter' puts C inside A CLAIM, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Acclaim is enthusiastic public praise, a strong form of approval.

clue.text: Double the food for such a dog

indicators.note: double means the word for food is written twice

parts.note: chow is slang for food

explanation.surface: A double helping of grub for a particular breed of dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed is a thick-coated Chinese dog with a blue-black tongue.

clue.text: A fruit, not cored, provides sustenance

parts.note: a lime is a citrus fruit

indicators.note: cored means the middle letter is removed, as an apple's core is

parts.note: taken as written before its centre goes

explanation.surface: An uncored piece of fruit is offered as food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cored' removes the central O of NOT, leaving NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliment is a formal word for food or nourishment.

clue.text: Obscure agreement included, not properly laid out

indicators.note: included means the word for agreement is put inside the word for obscure

parts.note: to mist something is to blur or obscure it
a deal is an agreement

explanation.surface: A vague agreement poorly set out in a contract.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand of cards wrongly distributed has been dealt out in error.

clue.text: Barely makes a run

parts.note: read as someone running naked across a public space, not someone narrowly managing a run

explanation.surface: Someone only just manages a run, perhaps in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: To streak is to dash naked through a public place, often a sports ground.

clue.text: Sign in front of church in West Midlands town

indicators.note: in front of places the sign before the church

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac
a minster is a large church

explanation.surface: A signpost outside a church in an English Midlands town.
explanation.walkthrough: LEOMINSTER (said 'Lemster') is a market town in Herefordshire, in England's West Midlands region.
explanation.definitionFit: The Herefordshire market town lies in the administrative region called the West Midlands.

clue.text: Writer showing courage to Americans

definitions.meaning: George ... was the pen name of the French novelist Aurore Dupin

explanation.surface: An author displaying bravery to a US audience.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the pen name of a French novelist; the other is US slang for grit and nerve.

clue.text: Drift off, spilling oil — see it and pass on

parts.note: to nap is to doze, to drift off to sleep

indicators.note: spilling scatters the letters of the word oil into a new order

explanation.surface: Dozing off and knocking over the oil bottle, then dying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilling' rearranges OIL into OLI. The definition plays on the saying 'See Naples and die'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian city is the subject of the proverb that you must see it before you die.

clue.text: Extension in credit facility provision

parts.note: taken as written
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
providing facility, that is ease or effortlessness

explanation.surface: A bank agrees to extend a customer's credit line.
explanation.walkthrough: Facility here means ease of doing something, not a building or a loan arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An extension of something is an enlargement or addition to it.

clue.text: Part of church where primate has installed saint

indicators.note: has installed means the abbreviation for saint is set inside the word for primate

parts.note: an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A church where a bishop has enthroned a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primate' suggests an archbishop, but it is an ape.
explanation.definitionFit: The apse is the vaulted semicircular recess at a church's east end.

clue.text: Cartoonist — a man, or it may appear so

indicators.note: may appear so says these letters, rearranged, can appear as the cartoonist

parts.note: the fodder letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A cartoonist's character might look like a man, or like an 'it'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may appear so' rearranges A MAN OR IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who draws animated cartoons brings drawn figures to life frame by frame.

clue.text: Summons the first lady's about to endorse

indicators.note: about means the possessive of the first lady goes around the word for endorse

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis, so her possessive gives EVES
to OK something is to approve or endorse it

explanation.surface: The President's wife is about to sign off on a legal summons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First lady' suggests a president's wife, but it is Eve, the first woman in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: To summon up a memory or feeling is to call it forth, to bring it to mind.

clue.text: Points dividing a scientist and film director

indicators.note: dividing means the compass points split the scientist's name

parts.note: Albert Einstein is the physicist
S and E are compass points, south and east

explanation.surface: Points of disagreement split a scientist and a filmmaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergei Eisenstein was the Soviet filmmaker behind Battleship Potemkin.
